questions.solution: A silent mutation is a change in the sequence of nucleotide bases which constitutes DNA, without a subsequent change in the amino acid or the function of the overall protein. Silent mutations are mutations in DNA that do not have an observable effect on the organism's phenotype.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is an example of an autosomal recessive disorder?
options: Colour blindness and sickle cell anaemia
questions.solution:
Phenylketonuria is an inborn error of metabolism inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. The affected individual lacks an enzyme that converts the amino acid phenylalanine into tyrosine. As a result of this, the phenylalanine gets accumulated and is converted into phenyl pyruvic acid and other derivatives. Accumulation of these in the brain results in mental retardation. These are also excreted through urine because of its poor absorption by the kidney.

Thalassemia is also an autosome-linked recessive blood disease transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are unaffected carriers for the gene (heterozygous). The defect could be due to either mutation or deletion which ultimately results in a reduced rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains (a and b chains) that make up hemoglobin. This causes the formation of abnormal hemoglobin molecules resulting in anemia which is characteristic of the disease.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An individual with Down's syndrome has _______ copies of 21<sup>st </sup>chromosome.
questions.solution: Down syndrome is usually caused by an error in cell division called "nondisjunction". Nondisjunction results in an embryo with three copies of chromosome 21 instead of the usual two. Prior to or at conception, a pair of 21st chromosomes in either the sperm or the egg fails to separate. As the embryo develops, the extra chromosome is replicated in every cell of the body. Thus Down syndrome is called trisomy of the 21<sup>st</sup> chromosome.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The example of the trait that is controlled by many genes in human beings is
questions.solution: The traits generally controlled by three or more genes are called as polygenic traits. Human skin colour is a classic example of this. In a polygenic trait, the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele, i.e, the effect of each allele is additive. To understand this better, let us assume that three genes A, B, C control skin colour in human, with the dominant forms A, B and C responsible for dark skin colour and the recessive forms a, b and c for light skin colour. The genotype with all the dominant alleles (AABBCC) will have the darkest skin colour and that with all the recessive alleles (aabbcc) will have the lightest skin colour. As expected, the genotype with three dominant alleles and three recessive alleles will have an intermediate skin colour.

questions.q: When a tall plant was self-pollinated, one-fourth of the progeny were dwarf. The genotypes of the parent and dwarf progenies are
questions.solution:
Dominance in genetics is a relationship between alleles of a gene, in which one allele masks the expression (phenotype) of another allele at the same locus. In this case, where a gene exists in two allelic forms (designated T and t). Allele T is dominant over t.

The genotype of a tall parent could be homozygous TT or heterozygous Tt. But, since on doing it’s self-cross, one-fourth of the progeny obtained has been found to be dwarf. Thus, its genotype must have been Tt.

The genotype of dwarf progeny would be tt. Allele t is recessive; therefore, it would be expressed only in the homozygous state.

Early use of the test cross was as an experimental mating test used to determine what alleles are present in the genotype. An organism's genetic makeup is called its genotype, and it reflects all of the alleles, or forms of the gene, that are carried by the organism. Consequently, a test cross can help determine whether a dominant phenotype is homozygous or heterozygous for a specific allele.

After crossing over, the resultant chromosomes are neither entirely maternal nor entirely paternal but contain genes from both parents. Synapsis and crossing over occur only in meiosis.

questions.solution: Crossing over, a process in genetics by which the two chromosomes of a homologous pair exchange equal segments with each other. A dihybrid cross describes a mating between two organisms that are identically hybrid for two traits, whereas a cross between two types of plants of the same species with the transmission of one character is called monohybrid cross.

A typical dihybrid cross AaBb x AaBb will produce 16 types of offsprings as follows:

Dihybrid genotypes: AaBb(4)

The Boveri–Sutton chromosomal theory of inheritance is a fundamental unifying theory of genetics. It identifies chromosomes as the carriers of genetic material. It correctly explains the mechanism underlying the laws of Mendelian inheritance by identifying chromosomes with the paired factors (particles) required by Mendel's laws. It also states that chromosomes are linear structures with genes located at specific sites called loci along with them.

The theory states that chromosomes, which are seen in all dividing cells and pass from one generation to the next, are the basis for all genetic inheritance.

Sutton and Boveri observed that the behaviour of chromosomes at meiosis can serve as the cellular basis of both segregation and independent assortment.

Cis arrangement means one chromosome has both dominant alleles and its homologous has both recessive alleles. Hence a condition where an individual heterozygous for two pairs of linked genes (AaBb) possesses the two dominant genes on one homologous chromosome pair and two recessive on the other it is said to be Cis arrangement.

Grasshopper is an example of an XO type of sex determination in which males have only one X chromosome beside autosomes, whereas females have a pair of X-chromosome. A large number of Insect show XO type of sex determination. While some of its sperm bear an X-chromosome and others do not have X-chromosome.

The XX/XY sex-determination system is the most familiar, as it is found in humans and Drosophila. In the system, females have two of the same kind of sex chromosome (XX), while males have two distinct sex chromosomes (XY).

The ZW sex-determination system is found in birds, reptiles, some insects and other organisms. The ZW sex-determination system is reversed compared to the XY system: females have two different kinds of chromosomes (ZW), and males have two of the same kind of chromosomes (ZZ).

questions.solution:
Klinefelter's syndrome is due to trisomy of sex (X) chromosomes. It is formed by the union of an abnormal XX egg and normal Y sperm or normal X egg and abnormal XY sperm. The individual has 47 chromosomes (44 + XXY). Such persons are sterile males (called feminized male) with undeveloped testes, mental retardation, female-like sparse body hair, and knock knees, long limbs and with some female characteristics such as feminine pitched voice and enlarged breasts (gynaecomastia).

Turner's syndrome occurs due to monosomy, i.e., (2n - 1). It is formed by the union of an abnormal 0 egg and a normal X sperm or a normal egg and an abnormal 0 sperm. The individual has 2n = 45 chromosomes (44 + X), instead of 46. Such individuals are sterile females who have rudimentary ovaries, undeveloped breasts, small uterus, puffy fingers, short stature (less than 5 feet), webbed neck, abnormal intelligence, cardiovascular abnormalities and hearing impairment.

questions.solution: The intergene distance on the chromosomes cannot be measured in the customary units employed in light microscopy; geneticists use an arbitrary unit to measure the map unit, to describe distances between linked genes. A map unit is equal to 1 per cent of crossovers (recombinants); that is, it represents the linear distance along the chromosome for which a recombination frequency of 1 per cent is observed. These distances can also be expressed in Morgan units; one Morgan unit represents 100 per cent crossing over. questions.solution:
Sickle cell anemia

- It is an autosomal recessive disease.

- This disease is controlled by a pair of alleles - HbA (normal dominant allele) and HbS (affected recessive allele).

- Both male and female have either of the three genotypes :

1. HbA HbA - Normal phenotype.

2. HbA HbS - Normal phenotype. For a heterozygous individual, there are 50% chances of transferring the affected allele to next progeny.

3. HbS  HbS - Diseased phenotype.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution:
A single gene product may produce more than one effect.
For example, starch synthesis in pea seeds is controlled by one gene. It has two alleles (B and b). Starch is synthesised effectively by BB homozygotes and therefore, large starch grains are produced. In contrast, bb homozygotes have lesser efficiency in starch synthesis and produce smaller starch grains. After maturation of the seeds, BB seeds are round and the bb seeds are wrinkled. Heterozygotes produce round seeds, and so B seems to be the dominant allele. But, the starch grains produced are of intermediate size in Bb seeds. So if starch grain size is considered as the phenotype, then from this angle, the alleles show incomplete dominance.

questions.solution:
The genotype of Alia will be XXc since she receives only one Xc chromosome (colourblindness chromosome) from her father. Ranbeer may be XY or XcY (since his mother is a carrier).

So we consider two possibilities:

1 .  Alia XXc and Ranbeer XY. In this, the daughters could be XX (not colourblind) or XXc (not colourblind)

2 .  Alia XXc and Ranbeer XcY. In this, the daughters could be XXc (not colourblind) or XcXc (colourblind)

Thus there is only 1 in 4 chance that their daughter will be colourblind.

Walter Sutton and Theodore Boveri noted that the behaviour of chromosomes was parallel to the behaviour of genes and used chromosome movement to explain Mendel's laws. Sex determination is the process of detecting the gender of the individual organism. In human, the sex of the individual is controlled by the 23 pair of chromosomes called sex chromosomes. If the individual has the pair combination as XY, he is a male and if the combination is XX, she is a female. Male in humans is heterogamous and produces two type of sperms cells whereas the female is homogamous, producing only one type of gamete -X. Sex of the zygote depends on the type of sperm cell fertilizing the egg cell.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When heterozygous tall plants are self -pollinated, then tall and dwarf plants are obtained. This explains
questions.solution:
As per Mendel's Law of segregation, "alleles segregate randomly into gametes: When gametes are formed, each allele of one parent segregates randomly into the gametes, such that half of the parent's gametes carry each allele."

Gametes are the reproductive cells produced by meiosis. These cells participate in the fertilization process to form the zygote. Gametes contain half the genetic content of the parent cell. Also, the genes/allele/loci segregate and recombine during the meiosis. The alleles in the gamete for the feature (stem height) segregate from each other and each gamete formed receives only one allele for each gene/feature.

Expression of tall and dwarf plants in next-generation on self-pollinating heterozygous tall plants supports the law of segregation.

Single gene was effectively regulating the multiple phenotypic expression - seed shape and starch synthesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mendel's law of independent assortment does NOT hold true for the genes that are located closely on
questions.solution: The chromosomes contain the genes for various features. If many genes are located on the same chromosome and within close proximity, the genes are considered to be linked. Such linked genes resist recombination during the meiotic phase of cell division in gamete formation and do not follow Mendel's law of independent assortment, which states that "that the alleles of two (or more) different genes get sorted into gametes independently of one another. In other words, the allele a gamete receives for one gene does not influence the allele received for another gene".

The disease sickle-cell anaemia is caused by the substitution of ___(i)____ by ____(ii)____ at the ____(iii)____ position of ____(iv)_____ globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule.

Which of the following CORRECTLY fills the blanks in the above statement?
questions.solution: Sickle cell anemia is a type of genetic blood disorder which is inherited from the parents. The person suffering from it develops an abnormal haemoglobin that leads to elongated and curved or sickle shaped RBC. Such condition occurs when the individual inherits two abnormal copies of gene for beta globin chain of haemoglobin from each parent. Normally, the red pigment molecule is made of four polypeptide chains two α-chains and two  <math><mi>β</mi></math> -chains. Sickle cell anaemia results in glutamic acid (Glu) is replaced by valine (Val) at sixth position in each of two  <math><mi>β</mi></math>  globin chain of haemoglobin. Such mutation is called as substitution mutation.

Such types of sex determination mechanism is designated to be the example of male heterogamety. In some other organisms, e.g., birds (like hens), a different mechanism of sex determination is observed. In this case the total number of chromosome is same in both males and females. But two different types of gametes in terms of the sex chromosomes, are produced by females, i.e., female heterogamety.

Monohybrid cross is defined as "a genetic mix between two individuals who have homozygous genotypes, or genotypes that have completely dominant or completely recessive alleles, which result in opposite phenotypes for a certain genetic trait". Polygenic inheritance is defined as characters which are determined by two or more gene pairs, and they have additive or cumulative effect. Such genes are called polygenes.

questions.solution:
Sickle cell anemia is a type of genetic blood disorder which is inherited from the parents. The person suffering from it develops an abnormal haemoglobin that leads to elongated and curved or sickle shaped RBC.

Such condition occurs when the individual inherits two abnormal copies of gene for beta globin chain of haemoglobin from each parent. The abnormal hemoglobin formed is not able to carry enough oxygen and this causes formation of rigid, non-liquid protein strands that distort the shape of the RBC.

Sickle cell anemia is a recessive autosomal gene disorder that follows Mendelian inheritance pattern.

questions.solution:
Genes are segments of DNA that make protein and facilitate the expression of characteristics.

A chromosome is a supercoiled and superfolded packaged DNA with attached proteins. The chromosomes contains the genes for various features. If many genes are located in the same chromosome and within close proximity, the genes are considered to be linked. Such linked genes resist recombination during the meiotic phase of cell division in gamete formation and tend to be transmitted together.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division results in the gain or loss of chromosomes, this is called as _____.
questions.solution:
When there is the presence of fewer or extra chromosomes than the normal genome number of the species is called aneuploidy (heteroploidy). During the gamete formation process by meiosis, there is a chance the two chromosomes of homologous pair do not separate resulting in one gamete will have an extra chromosome (N + 1) while the other becomes deficient in one chromosome (N-1). This results in aneuploidy. The resulting zygote either will be deficient in chromosomes or has additional chromosomes. 

Aneuploidy can also be defined as the presence of an abnormal number of chromosomes in a cell, for example, a human cell having 45 or 47 chromosomes instead of the usual 46.

questions.solution:
Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment states that "when two or more characteristics are inherited, individual hereditary factors assort independently during gamete production, giving different traits an equal opportunity of occurring together."

When two or more different genes are located to close to each other in a chromosome are said to be linked. Linked gene are found to avoid recombination and are not assorted during gamete production.

Linked genes are in contradiction to the Law of independent assortment thus, if Mendel had known about linkage during his experiments, he would have not been able to explain the inheritance of two genes without one affecting the other.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Cystic fibrosis is a/an
questions.solution:
Mendelian disorders are mainly determined by alteration or mutation in the single gene. These disorders are transmitted to the offspring on the same lines as we have studied in the principle of inheritance. The pattern of inheritance of such Mendelian disorders can be traced in a family by the pedigree analysis. Most common and prevalent Mendelian disorders are Haemophilia, Cystic fibrosis, Sickle-cell anaemia, Colour blindness, Phenylketonuria, Thalassemia, etc.
Cystic fibrosis, sickle-cell anaemia and phenylketonuria are examples of autosomal recessive disorders, while haemophilia and colour blindness are sex-linked disorders (both of them are X-linked recessive disorders). Examples of autosomal dominant includes myotonic dystrophy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Haplodiploidy is found in
questions.solution: The phenomenon where an unfertilized egg develops into a male and the fertilized egg forms a female is called Haploid-diploid mechanism or Haplodiploidy. In such scenario, female is diploid and male is haploid. Also, the sperm cells are formed by mitosis and female eggs by meiosis. If the egg is not fertilized, it will still develop but into a male (arrhenotoky or arrhenotokous parthenogenesis). It is commonly observed in insects, such as bees, wasps, saw flies and ants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding the pedigree analysis.
options: Square represents male in the pedigree chart.
It is useful for genetic counselling.
It is an analysis of traits in several generations of a family.
questions.solution: The pedigree analysis provides information regarding the inheritance of particular traits or diseases and using it we can predict the possibility of appearance of any traits in the new generation. In it, the solid symbols represent affected individuals and empty/non-solid symbols show unaffected individuals. For female, a circle is used and a square represents male.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The genetically inactive and highly condensed region with tightly packed DNA which receives dark stain is
questions.solution: Heterochromatin is a tightly packed form of DNA or condensed DNA, which comes in multiple varieties. These varieties lie on a continuum between the two extremes of constitutive heterochromatin and facultative heterochromatin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match Column- I with Column - II and select the CORRECT option from the codes given below
 
  Column I   Column II
(1) A single trait controlled by three or more than three alleles (i) Pleiotropy
(2) A single trait controlled by three or more than three genes (ii) Multiple alleles
(3) A single gene exhibits multiple phenotypic expression (iii) Polygenic inheritance
questions.solution:
Multiple alleles is a condition where more than two variants of the gene occupy the same locus. Mutation is change in the sequence of DNA segment. Mutation in the sequence of amino acids can result in formation of a new allele if the changes are simple and not on many bases. Multiple alleles combine in different combination to produce different phenotypes. Such variation in phenotypes occur due to the proteins encoded by the allele combination.

When traits are controlled by three or more genes, they are called polygenic traits and their inheritance is called as polygenic inheritance. Human skin colour is a classic example following polygenic inheritance as the skin colour is regulated by three pairs of gene. Polygenic inheritance is influenced by the environment as well and not just the polygenes.

Gene is a segment of DNA responsible for expression of proteins which in true expresses the character or feature represented by the gene. When this gene is regulating the expression of more than one feature in an organism such phenomenon is called pleiotropy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The pleiotropic character represents that quality of gene in which it can
options: be capable of representing more than one form
regulate more than one phenotypic characters
questions.solution: A gene which can regulate and express multiple phenotypic characters is called a pleiotropic gene. The underlying mechanism of pleiotropy in most cases is the effect of a gene on metabolic pathways which contribute towards different phenotypes. An example of this is the disease phenylketonuria, which occurs in humans.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the given statements is NOT CORRECT regarding colour blindness?
options: It is more common in males than in females.
Homozygous recessive condition is required for the expression of colour blindness in females.
Males can be carriers of the trait.
Colour blind women always have a colourblind father and always produce a colour blind son.
questions.solution:
X-linked disorders are inherent disorders due to mutation in the X-chromosome which causes the phenotype to be always expressed in male and in female only in homozygous condition.

Colour blindness is a X-linked recessive disorder. In colour blindness, the affected individual is not able to distinguish colour especially red and green.

The son will always be colour blind if he has a colour blind mother.

Since the affected chromosome is X chromosome and not Y, the only female can be carriers in heterozygous condition.

Such an individual has overall masculine development, however, the feminine development (development of breast, i.e., Gynaecomastia) is also expressed. Such individuals are sterile.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the recombination percentage between gene y and w in Drosophila?
questions.solution: The recombination frequency of the test cross progeny is always lower than 50%. Therefore, if any two genes are completely linked, their recombination frequency is almost 0%. The phenomenon of linkage was studied by the scientist T.H. Morgan using the common fruit fly or Drosophila melanogaster.

Pedigree analysis provides information regarding inheritance of particular traits or diseases and using it we can predict the possibility of appearance of any traits in the new generation.

Member 3 is unaffected and the normal condition is recessive thus its genotype will be pp. To obtain recessive homozygous condition, both parents must have the recessive allele, therefore, member 2 must be heterozygous as it is affected one. Genotype of member 2 is Pp.

Member 1 genotype is also Pp as the son is unaffected (pp) and the wife of member 1 is normal.

questions.solution: Colour blindness is a X-linked recessive disorder. In it, the affected individual has is not able to distinguish colour especially read and green. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following sets of phenomena leads to variation in DNA?
questions.solution: A mutation refers to a change in the nucleotide sequence of a short region of DNA. On the other hand, recombination reconstructs a part of the genome. The main difference between mutation and recombination is that mutation brings a small-scale rearrangement in the genome whereas recombination brings a large-scale rearrangement in the genome. Both are responsible for evolution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following trait shows transmission from carrier female to male progeny?
questions.solution: In humans, inheritance of X-linked recessive traits follows a unique pattern made up of three points. The first is that affected fathers cannot pass X-linked recessive traits to their sons because fathers give Y chromosomes to their sons. This means that males affected by an X-linked recessive disorder that is inherited will be from X chromosome of their mothers. Second, X-linked recessive traits are more commonly expressed in males than females.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Loss or gain of a segment of DNA results in
questions.solution: Chromosomal aberration or chromosomal abnormalities occurs when there is a defect in the number of chromosomes in a cell of an organism or in the arrangement of genetic material (genes) on the chromosome, the top four types of chromosomal aberrations. The types are 1. Deficiency or deletion 2. Duplication 3. Translocation 4. Inversion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Starch grain in pea plant shows
questions.solution: Starch grain size in pea is controlled by gene Bb which in the dominant state produces an enzyme starch debranching enzyme (SBE). Starch is synthesized effectively by BB homozygotes and therefore large grains are produced. In bb, homozygous have lesser efficiency in starch synthesis and produce smaller starch grains. In Bb heterozygous condition starch grains produces are intermediate in size thus shows incomplete dominance.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Turner's syndrome in humans is caused by:
questions.solution: Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division cycle results in the gain or loss of a chromosome(s), called aneuploidy. For example, Down’s syndrome results in the gain of extra copy of chromosome 21. Similarly, Turner’s syndrome results due to loss of an X chromosome in human females.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following characters was not chosen by Mendel?
questions.solution: Johann Mendel, considered as the father of genetics, gave the observation and theories of inheritance of characteristics. He made his conclusions bases on experiments conducted on Pisum sativum, pea plant. In the plant he had considered seven characteristics - seed shape, seed colour, pod shape, pod colour, stem height, flower colour, flower position/location.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Alleles that produce independent effects in their heterozygous condition are called:
questions.solution:
Codominance is a condition in which both alleles of a gene pair in heterozygote are fully expressed, with neither one being dominant or recessive to the other.
Epistasis is the suppression of the normal phenotypic of the gene by a non-allelic gene.
Complimentary genes are two independent genes present on different gene loci which assist each other in expressing a trait.
Supplementary genes are two independent genes present on different gene loci, each of may produce its own trait and interact when present together in dominant state to produce a new trait.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A couple had two sons, one was colour blind while the other wasn't. They also had a colour blind daughter. Which statement about this couple is true?
options: Husband is colour blind but wife is not
Husband is normal and wife is colour blind
Husband and wife both are colour blind
Husband and wife both are normal
questions.solution: Colour blind man has one X chromosome with the gene for colour blindness which he receives from his mother. His colour blind sister has two X chromosomes each with the gene for colour blindness. She has received one of these from her father and one from her mother. Thus from this information we can conclude that their father is colour blind and their mother has at least one X chromosome for colour blindness. Also they have a normal brother. That means their mother has one X chromosome without colour blindness genes. Hence mother is a carrier.

A Rh-ve child from A Rh-ve mother and O Rh-ve father
AB Rh+ve child from A Rh+ve mother and B Rh-ve father
O Rh-ve child from O Rh-ve mother and O Rh-ve father
questions.solution:
Rh antigen follows normal Mendelian inheritance. If 'R' is the allele which produces Rhesus antigen and 'r' is the allele which doesn't, then a person with Rh+ve blood group can be RR or Rr while a person with Rh-ve blood group will always be rr (always homozygous). Person with A blood group may have genotype IAIA or IAIO. A person with AB blood group has genotype IAIB. A person with blood group O has genotype IOIO (always homozygous)

If the person is heterozygous for both blood group systems, genotype should be IAIB Rr (AB Rh+ve child)

options: may be same or greater but never lesser than
questions.solution: In a monohybrid cross, there are two monohybrids out of total of four offsprings. (AA: Aa: aa =1 :2 :1). Thus their proportion is 50%. In a dihybrid cross, there are four dihybrids out of total sixteen offsprings. (AABB: AAbb: aaBB: aabb: AaBB: AABb: Aabb: aaBb : AaBb = 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 : 2 : 2: 2 : 2 : 4). Thus their proportion is 25%.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The genetic disorders in which the patients have one chromosome less than normal humans are:
questions.solution: The presence of an extra chromosome in diploid chromosome number is called trisomy. It is represented by  <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>.</mo></math>  Here the patient has 47 chromosomes instead of 46. It is represented by  <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> .Thus they have 45 chromosomes. Turner's syndrome is due to absence of one X chromosome in females. The patient's cells contain only one X chromosome instead of two. Thus their genotype is represented by  <math><mo>(</mo><mn>44</mn><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mo>)</mo></math> . Thalassemia is a disorder of genes and not whole chromosomes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Sickle cell-anaemia disorder arises due to
options: duplication of a segment of DNA
substitution in a single base of DNA
deletion of a segment of DNA
duplication in a base pair of RNA
questions.solution:
Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a group of blood disorders typically inherited from a person's parents. The most common type is known as sickle cell anaemia (SCA). It results in an abnormality in the oxygen-carrying protein haemoglobin found in red blood cells.

A classical example of point mutation is a change of single base pair in the gene for beta globin chain that results in the change of amino acid residue glutamate to valine. It results in a diseased condition called as sickle cell anemia.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Select one word to describe the following statements and choose the correct option.

a. If F1 resembled either of the two parents
b. If F1 resembled both the parents
c. If F1 did not resemble either of the two parents and was in between the two
questions.solution: If member of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> generation resembles phenotypically with any parent (dominant parent) then this phenomenon is said to be Dominance. If member of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> generation carries characters of both the parents then this phenomenon is said to be Co-dominance. questions.solution: Sickle cell anemia is a recessive autosomal gene disorder that follows Mendelian inheritance pattern. Sickle cell anemia is a type of genetic blood disorder which is inherited from the parents. The person suffering from it develops an abnormal haemoglobin that leads to elongated and curved or sickle shaped RBC. Such condition occurs when the individual inherits two abnormal copies of gene for beta globin chain of haemoglobin from each parent. Normally, the red pigment molecule is made of four polypeptide chains two α-chains and two <math><mi>β</mi></math> -chains. Sickle cell anaemia results in glutamic acid (Glu) is replaced by valine (Val) at sixth position in each of two <math><mi>β</mi></math> globin chain of haemoglobin. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During his experiments with Drosophila, Morgan discovered that
options: the genes for linkage were located on the Y-chromosome.
if two genes in a dihybrid cross were situated on the same chromosome, the proportion of non-parental gene combinations were much higher than the parental type.
the distance between genes couldn't be measured using the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome.
when genes were grouped on the same chromosome, very tightly linked genes showed very low recombination while loosely linked genes showed higher recombination.
questions.solution:
Morgan and his group also found that even when genes were grouped on the same chromosome, some genes were very tightly linked (showed very low recombination) while others were loosely linked (showed higher recombination). For example he found that the genes white and yellow were very tightly linked and showed only 1.3 per cent recombination while white and miniature wing showed 37.2 per cent recombination.
The genes for linkage were located on the X chromosome and when the two genes in a dihybrid cross were situated on the same chromosome, the proportion of parental gene combinations were much higher than the non-parental type. 
Morgan's student Alfred Sturtevant used the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure of the distance between genes and ‘mapped’ their position on the chromosome.

questions.solution:
When traits are controlled by three or more genes, they are called polygenic traits and their inheritance is called as polygenic inheritance. Polygenic inheritance is influenced by the environment as well and not just the polygenes.

Kernel colour of wheat is regulated AA and BB that is two pairs of genes. Genes A and B express the red colour of kernel. They are dominant over their recessive alleles. When a red kernel wheat variety is crossed with white kernel wheat, the ratio obtained in F2 is 1 : 4 : 6 : 4 : 1 due to the polygenic inheritance.

two- thirds of the total number of chromosomes
questions.solution: The tendency of genes present on the same chromosome to be inherited together is called linkage. All the genes on a chromosome are said to be linked to one another and belong to the same linkage group. Number of linkage groups of a particular species corresponds to its haploid number of chromosomes or number of pairs of chromosomes. E.g. Pisum has 14 chromosomes thus it has seven linkage groups.

could not be predicted with reference to w and m
questions.solution:
T. H. Morgan proposed the chromosomal theory of linkage, he experimented on Drosophila melanogaster (Fruitfly). In Cross A he took 2 genes y and w which are about 1.3 map unit distant from each other so he obtained 98.7% parental characters (due to higher linkage) and 1.3% recombinant characters.

In Cross B, he took 2 genes w and m genee which are about 37.2 map unit distant from each other, so he obtained 62.8% parental characters (due to comparatively lesser linkage) and 37.2% recombinant characters.

Morgan and his students have found that linked genes show varied recombinations, some being more tightly linked than others, (i) In Drosophila, the crossing of yellow bodied (y) and white-eyed (w) female with brown bodied (y+) red-eyed (w+) male-produced F1 to be brown bodied and red-eyed females, while males were yellow bodied and white eyed. questions.solution: Sickle cell anaemia is an autosome linked recessive trait that can be transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are a carrier for the gene (or heterozygous). The defect is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta-globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. questions.solution: Sickle cell anaemia is a severe hereditary form of anaemia in which a mutated form of haemoglobin distorts the red blood cells into a crescent shape. It is common among people of African descent. The mutation (transversion/single point mutation) causing sickle cell anaemia is a single nucleotide substitution (A to T) in the codon for amino acid 6. The change converts a glutamic acid codon (GAG) to a valine codon (GTG). The form of haemoglobin in persons with sickle cell anaemia is referred to as HbS.
